summary: Contrastive GOOD-vs-BAD few-shot on RAG base
hypothesis: Prepending a GOOD-vs-BAD worked example should teach the model which anti-patterns to avoid better than positive-only demos or instruction checklists, because the contrast directly demonstrates the failure modes the judge flags rather than just showing success cases.
technique: Built on exp003's RAG positive few-shot single-call pipeline, but prepended one fixed contrastive worked example on a neutral non-eval task ("Organize my garage") whose WEAK set demonstrates the exact anti-patterns flagged by the judge (restating facts, off-task questions, vague filler, compound asks, redundant pairs). No extra model calls — the contrast is baked into the prompt as a negative demonstration.

stages.text: Single call with contrastive GOOD/BAD prompt
